```{r}

print(result)
```

```{r}
#Part B4

x <- 10

if (x > 5) {
  print("A")       # This condition is checked first
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}

# x is 10, which satisfies x > 5 immediately.
# R executes the FIRST true condition and skips all remaining branches.
# Even though x > 8 is also true, it is never reached because
# the if else if chain stops at the first match.
```

```{r}
#Part B5

#if is a control flow statement that works on a single condition and executes a block of code based on whether that one condition is TRUE or FALSE. ifelse() is a vectorized function that checks a condition across every element of a vector at once and returns a value for each element.

#You would choose if when making a single decision in your code, such as checking one variable and deciding what to do next. You would choose ifelse() when you need to apply a condition across an entire vector and return a result for each element
```

```{r}

                       na.strings = c("", "NA", "N/A"))
```

```{r}
} else {
  print("File not found. Please check the file path or working directory.")
}
```

```{r}
#Part C6F1

students$FinalGrade <- (0.30 * students$Quiz) +
                       (0.30 * students$Midterm) +
                       (0.40 * students$Final)

students[, c("Name", "Quiz", "Midterm", "Final", "FinalGrade")]
```

```{r}
#Part C6F2

students$Result <- ifelse(is.na(students$FinalGrade), NA,
                   ifelse(students$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed"))

students[, c("Name", "FinalGrade", "Result")]
```

```{r}
#Part C6F3

students$Remarks <- ifelse(is.na(students$FinalGrade), NA,
                    ifelse(students$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
                    ifelse(students$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
                    ifelse(students$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
                    ifelse(students$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair",
                                                      "Needs Improvement")))))

students[, c("Name", "FinalGrade", "Remarks")]
```

```{r}
#Part C6F4

students$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(students$Attendance < 80, "At Risk", "OK")

students[, c("Name", "Attendance", "AttendanceFlag")]
```

```{r}
#Part C6F5

students$Honors <- ifelse(is.na(students$FinalGrade), "No",
                   ifelse(students$FinalGrade >= 90 & students$Attendance >= 90,
                          "Yes", "No"))

students[, c("Name", "FinalGrade", "Attendance", "Honors")]
```

```{r}

  } else {
```

```{r}
#Part D7B

at_risk <- students[students$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]

if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  print(paste("At-risk file exported:", nrow(at_risk), "student(s) listed."))
} else {
  print("No at-risk students found. File was not created.")
}
```

```{r}
#Part D7C

honors_rows <- students$Honors == "Yes" & !is.na(students$Honors)

honors <- students[honors_rows, c("StudentID", "Name", "Section",
                                   "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]

if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
  print(paste("Honors list exported:", nrow(honors), "student(s) listed."))
} else {
  print("No honors candidates found. File was not created.")
}

honors
```

```{r}
#Part D7D

if (all(dim(check_full) == dim(students))) {
  print("Full table verified: dimensions match.")

  print("Warning: dimensions do not match. Check the export.")
}

# Read back and compare at-risk file
check_risk <- read.csv("at_risk_students.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

if (nrow(check_risk) == nrow(at_risk)) {
  print("At-risk file verified: row count matches.")
} else {
  print("Warning: at-risk row count does not match.")
}

# Read back and compare honors file
check_honors <- read.csv("honors_list.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

if (nrow(check_honors) == nrow(honors)) {
  print("Honors file verified: row count matches.")
} else {
  print("Warning: honors row count does not match.")
}

# Preview each file
head(check_full)
head(check_risk)
head(check_honors)
```

```{r}
#Part D10.1

# Because NA >= 75 does not return FALSE, it returns NA. This means ifelse() cannot evaluate the condition and may assign the wrong label or produce unexpected NA results in the output column. Checking is.na() first intercepts the missing value before any numeric comparison is attempted.
```

```{r}
#Part D10.2

#The student with the missing FinalGrade (NA) would be labeled "Failed" instead of "Incomplete", because NA >= 75 returns NA which ifelse() treats as FALSE, falling through to the "Failed" branch.
```

```{r}
#Part D10.3

#ifelse() is better when applying a condition across an entire vector, such as labeling all 15 students at once, because it is vectorized and handles every element in one call. if-else is better when making a single decision in your script, such as checking whether a file exists or whether a data frame is empty, because it evaluates exactly one TRUE or FALSE value and controls the flow of the program accordingly.
```

```{r}
#Part D10.4

#Exporting without errors does not guarantee the file contents are correct. Reading it back lets you verify the dimensions, column names, and values match the original data frame, catching silent issues such as extra columns from row names, missing rows, or NA values that were written incorrectly.
```
